habitat: Dry, rocky ground with short grass, open fields and open areas within woodland, and little-developed urban areas. It rests by day under bushes or among rocks.
summary: A common resident thick-knee of dry open ground. The upperparts are buff and heavily streaked and spotted dark brown. The underparts are white, with a blackish-streaked chest. The eye is yellow, the bill is yellow with a black tip, and the legs are long and yellow. It has no wing-bar. The night call is a shrill, eerie chwee-chwee that trails off. The sexes and the immature are not separated in this account.

similar.note: Water Thick-knee has a grey wing-bar edged black and keeps to river and lake banks. Spotted Thick-knee is heavily spotted above and has no wing-bar.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.

head.pattern: Buffy above, with dark brown streaking.

upperparts.pattern: Heavily streaked and spotted dark brown.

underparts.pattern: White below, the chest streaked blackish.

viewNotes.note: Heavily spotted buff upperparts, yellow legs and a yellow bill with a black tip, on dry open ground.
Yellow eye and the black-tipped yellow bill.
No wing-bar. A separate upperwing flight pattern was not named.
White underparts. The underwing was not named.

calls.description: A shrill, eerie chwee-chwee, chwee-chwee, chwee, chwee, chwee, tiu-tiu-tiu, trailing off, mostly on moonlit nights. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from a Bloemfontein garden. The filename is a date stamp. No playable grade A from Kruger outranked it.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident. Chick down, a sex difference and a flight photograph are gaps. The call is grade A from the Free State.
